steps.say: Metastases are the commonest brain tumours in adults, and meningioma is the commonest primary tumour. Primary central nervous system lymphoma is rare but critical, because steroids melt it and spoil biopsy. Each group behaves differently, so the first job is to place the lesion correctly from its scan appearance.
steps.tx: **Brain metastases** are the commonest brain tumours in adults, and **meningioma** is the commonest primary brain tumour. **Primary CNS lymphoma** is uncommon but critical because steroids melt it and spoil biopsy. Lung, breast and melanoma cause most metastases. Multiple lesions at grey white junctions favour metastases, while a dural based mass favours meningioma.

steps.say: Meningioma arises from arachnoid cap cells and grows slowly over years. Most are World Health Organisation grade one and benign. Higher grades invade brain and recur. Women are affected about twice as often as men, and prior cranial radiation is the strongest risk factor. Multiple tumours point to neurofibromatosis type two.
steps.tx: **Meningioma** arises from arachnoid cap cells and is usually **WHO grade 1** and benign. Grades 2 and 3 invade brain and recur after surgery. Women are affected twice as often as men. Prior **cranial radiation** is the strongest risk factor, and multiple meningiomas suggest **neurofibromatosis type 2**. Seizures with a slow focal deficit are typical.

steps.say: Steroids shrink primary central nervous system lymphoma within days, so you must biopsy before giving them. It is centred on the ventricles and gives even enhancement with restricted diffusion. The eyes are involved in about one in five cases, so slit lamp review is routine. Young patients need HIV testing, and the body is staged to prove there is no systemic disease.
steps.tx: **Primary CNS lymphoma** is a diffuse large B cell lymphoma of brain, eye and cord. It enhances **homogeneously** around the ventricles and melts with **steroids**, so biopsy must come first. Slit lamp examination finds **ocular involvement** in 1 in 5 cases. Most patients are immunocompetent and older, while young patients need **HIV** testing.

steps.say: A metastasis presents with headache, seizures or a stroke like deficit that evolves over days to weeks. Lung cancer is the commonest source, then breast, melanoma, kidney and colon. Melanoma and kidney deposits bleed, so sudden worsening suggests haemorrhage into the tumour. Finding the primary decides drugs and prognosis.
steps.tx: **Metastases** present with headache, seizures or a rapidly progressive focal deficit. **Lung** is the commonest primary, then breast, melanoma, renal and colorectal. **Melanoma**, renal, thyroid and choriocarcinoma bleed into their deposits. A solitary lesion needs a **chest CT** and primary hunt, since systemic therapy now drives survival.

steps.say: Contrast M R I is the first test for any suspected brain tumour, and it separates these three reliably. Meningioma is seen as a dural tail that compresses rather than invades brain. Lymphoma is seen as even enhancement with restricted diffusion. Metastases show much swelling for their size, and guided biopsy decides doubtful cases.
steps.tx: **Contrast MRI** is the first test and separates the three reliably. A **dural tail** with compression favours meningioma. **Homogeneous enhancement** with diffusion restriction favours lymphoma. **Disproportionate oedema** around small lesions favours metastases. **MR spectroscopy** shows high choline in tumour, and **stereotactic biopsy** decides doubtful cases.

steps.say: Symptomatic meningioma is removed surgically, aiming for a Simpson grade one resection. Small tumours without symptoms are simply watched with yearly scans. Radiation follows incomplete removal and all grade two and three tumours. Systemic therapy is a salvage option only, and seizures are treated with antiseizure drugs while oedema needs short course dexamethasone.
steps.tx: **Surgery** with Simpson grade 1 removal cures most symptomatic meningiomas. Small **asymptomatic** tumours need yearly MRI surveillance only. **Radiotherapy** follows subtotal resection and all grade 2 and 3 tumours. **Systemic therapy** is salvage only and rarely helps. Seizures need **antiseizure therapy**, and oedema needs short course **dexamethasone**.

steps.say: Whole brain radiation alone for metastases is now the past. One to four lesions are treated with focused stereotactic radiosurgery, which protects memory better. Surgery is for large lesions, diagnostic doubt, or posterior fossa mass effect. Driver mutations changed everything, because pills such as E G F R inhibitors treat brain and body together in mutation positive lung cancer.
steps.tx: **Stereotactic radiosurgery** is first line for 1 to 4 metastases and preserves cognition better than whole brain radiotherapy. **Surgery** suits lesions above 3 cm, diagnostic doubt and posterior fossa mass effect. **Targeted pills** such as EGFR inhibitors control brain disease in mutation positive lung cancer. **Whole brain radiotherapy** is now reserved for numerous lesions and leptomeningeal spread.

nodes.label: Whole brain radiation only if widespread

steps.say: Methotrexate in high doses is the backbone of primary CNS lymphoma treatment, not the C H O P regimen used in systemic disease. In fit young patients, combined chemotherapy is added to the methotrexate backbone. Whole brain radiation is avoided in the elderly because it causes delayed dementia. Relapse after two years still responds to retreatment, which is unusual among brain tumours.
steps.tx: **High dose methotrexate** above 3 g per sq m is the backbone of CNS lymphoma therapy. **Combined chemotherapy** is added to methotrexate in fit young patients. **Whole brain radiotherapy** is deferred in the elderly because of delayed **neurotoxicity**. **Autologous transplant** consolidates young fit patients. **Steroids** alone never count as treatment because relapse is rapid.

steps.say: Outcome follows the primary cancer more than the brain lesion count. Lung and melanoma with brain spread live months without drugs and years with targeted therapy. Meningioma grade one is cured by full removal in most cases. Lymphoma responds fast but recurs, and age with performance status predicts survival best. Prognosis is always quoted by group, never as one number.
steps.tx: **Prognosis** follows the primary and the group, not lesion count alone. Fully removed grade 1 meningioma recurs in under 1 in 10 cases. CNS lymphoma median survival is measured in **years** with methotrexate regimens. Metastasis survival ranges from **months** without systemic control to **years** with targeted therapy. **Performance status** predicts outcome best.

steps.say: Examiners love the steroid trap in lymphoma, the dural tail in meningioma, and the bleed prone metastasis. Multiple lesions indicate metastases until proven otherwise, and one dural lesion indicates meningioma. Do not irradiate the whole brain first when radiosurgery is suitable. And never call glioblastoma the commonest tumour overall, because metastases are commoner than it.
steps.tx: **Exam traps:** steroids before biopsy destroy the lymphoma diagnosis, and **whole brain radiotherapy** is wrong when 1 to 4 lesions suit radiosurgery. **Multiple lesions** mean metastases first, a **dural tail** means meningioma, and **even periventricular enhancement** means lymphoma. **Melanoma** deposits bleed. Metastases outnumber **glioblastoma** overall.

points: Metastases: many small lesions, oedema, known primary
left.title: Metastases

points: Lymphoma: single even lesion, melts with steroids, biopsy first
right.title: Primary CNS lymphoma

steps.say: For the exam, lock in the ranking of metastases first and meningioma first among primaries, the dural tail, the steroid biopsy trap, high dose methotrexate, and radiosurgery for few lesions. Numbers carry marks, so memorise the six to ten facts in this table exactly as written and recall which scan sign belongs to which tumour.
steps.tx: **High yield for the exam:** metastases are commonest overall and meningioma commonest primary. Dural tail marks meningioma, even periventricular enhancement marks lymphoma, and grey white junction deposits mark metastases. High dose methotrexate treats lymphoma, radiosurgery treats few metastases, and steroids must follow biopsy.

title: Meningioma, CNS Lymphoma, Metastases and Other Tumours
